reviews.title: Offer of Free Month Charged me Immediately
reviews.text:
I have tried insight timer on and off for years.  I absolutely despise all the hoop jumping to get to the main menu… all my goals, and consecutive days, and good job; super tedious and unnecessary. The user interface is super confusing as well; no easy way to see what you like, your playlists etc. 

Recently, I was looking for something specific and went back on it to see if they had what I wanted.  While I was there it offered me a free month, so I thought, that’s generous, why not? So I agreed. 

 Within minutes my card was charged for year and no free month. Guess who has to then figure out how to request a refund?  

I did this through both apple and insight timer.  Insight timer offered no help, and no month free, just a lot of words of concern.  Apple did, after 24 hours, refund my money, but I also lost my supposed free month.  

Be wary. What a total waste of time.

reviews.title: Stupid log in
reviews.text: I already have a PAID account and every time I have to sign it the app requires you to go through an onboarding process.  Why?

reviews.title: Keeps getting Worse…
reviews.text:
Latest Update someone named “Christopher” is overriding my system settings and autoplaying in a video speaking. 

If my music stops and i hit play again, I get Christopher again, not my music. 

When a track ends my practice is interrupted again with a celebration that I use the app every day - thanks - I know?! .. the celebration cannot be turned off or bypassed to access the next track.. 

Their solution was to continue quitting the app and restarting lol why not resolve these issues? 

I have been wondering which device was malfunctioning for 3 days now. I don’t listen to audio speaking. Yet a have a random man’s voice coming through my speakers unexpectedly in my home, alarming me, rather than allowing me to relax, and meditate - which was once the whole point of this app.

reviews.title: Intrusive Questioning
reviews.text:
This review is specifically about the intrusive questions and apparent use of AI to “design a programme”.  Most importantly, the fact that you cannot use the app without completing a long list of questions is unacceptable.
For an app that is promoting trauma-informed practice, this lack of consent and choice is out of integrity.  Personally, I clicked through any old answers just to use the app, so the questions were useless and the AI process wasted resources creating a meaningless plan. 

Please make this process consensual with the option to opt out.

reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: This app literally saved my life. But the past couple of weeks have frustrated me to the point of deleting the app. Constant updates so you can’t find anything, video summaries instead of written (everytime I open the app, I am bombarded with these videos) and now having to pay for meditations. Such a shame it became all about money.

reviews.title: Stop the gamification of meditation
reviews.text: I have subscribed to Insight Timer for more than 10 years. I used to love it. Now, logging on requires me to answer 1 million questions about my goals and interests. It wants to set up targets and competitions and reminders. I just want to freaking meditate. What used to be the most straightforward meditation app became the biggest three ring circus and I couldn’t be more disappointed. I’m sure it makes the developers more money this way, so enjoy.

reviews.title: Can’t stand it anymore
reviews.text: Doesn’t properly track your usage then resets your streaks incorrectly daily now. So unbelievably aggravating it is the exact opposite of relaxing and even more mind blowing for an app supposedly based around soothing you, you literally can’t even just fully turn off this gamification!!!! As soon as my subscription is done I won’t renew sadly after many years using. Contacted support multiple times and they are beyond useless and doing nothing to resolve this clear fundamental fault.

reviews.title: Almost the best meditation app
reviews.text: They don’t let you customize the consecutive day timer and it’s just not nearly customizable enough. There’s nobody working in the product team it seems like.

reviews.title: AI is ruining IS
reviews.text: I have been a paid subscriber to this app for years and am sorry to say that the experience is being ruined by AI, with no way to avoid it as far as I can tell. BTW you are automatically opted in to having your info mined by AI.

reviews.title: Can’t cancel
reviews.text: The app won’t let me cancel the subscription, and there’s no support.

reviews.title: Content good, app mediocre
reviews.text: The variety of guided meditations and resources is good and they’ve clearly put some effort into that. But the interface is really horrible. Difficult to navigate difficult to find things really just cluttered, messy, and quite frankly stress inducing, which is counterproductive.

reviews.title: To many pop ups
reviews.text: This app is okay. I feel like there are AI led meditations.  There are way to many pop ups or questions. Just let me find my peace and leave me alone with all these questions!

reviews.title: Videos - Negative
reviews.text: Incredibly disappointing a meditation app is now using social media gimmicks to distract and entrap users. My favorited teachers are hidden, onslaught of input, forced to constantly expand my “community”. Shame.

reviews.title: Hate the update
reviews.text: Hate the focus on videos. Hate the aggressiveness towards operating like social media and being pumped a feed. The point of this app has been grounding and getting away from those kinds of things in life where we cannot escape them. Terrible to have added them here. Hate hate hate hate that I can no longer listen to a brief preview in the list screen, cannot believe it forces me to go to a detail screen and tries to get me stuck in a scroll of other previews. A truly repulsive approach. Were you recently purchased by PE or something?

reviews.title: Wastes your time with forced engagement
reviews.text: Used to use this app daily.  Then they started forcing engagement with questions and emotion check ins. These are obnoxious and time wasting.  Only get this app if you want to lose time daily to a wellness corporation.

reviews.title: Really pushy agenda makes the app terrible to use, wish that wasn’t the case
reviews.text: The app is incredibly frustrating to use due to its relentless efforts to categorize users, push them to set up schedules and goals whether they want to or not, and then shower them with unwanted screens asking them to say “I’m committed” and engage with the product every day.  Once in a great while, I’ll use the app for something specific.  But I almost don’t even want to try!  The experience outside of the actual teaching is so bad for me.  Check out other reviews to see what I mean.  I would want to give the app 3 stars because I’ve benefited from it.  But the fact that Insight Timer doesn’t listen to feedback and change their ways means I’m going to leave a 1 star review with the goal of having more impact on the overall rating.

reviews.title: Let us skip intro questions
reviews.text: PLEASE stop forcing users to run through goal setting questions every time we open the app. Let us skip or actually remember our answers. I just want to open the app and pull up a meditation occasionally. I don’t need or want to answer 15 pages of questions first

reviews.title: Too gamified for me
reviews.text: I have a few meditation apps and this one is by far the most gamified, mainstream, over produced one. I dont care about streaks, i just want the ability to open an app, pick a session, and listen to it. Its also very controlling. You can’t rewind in a session unless youre a paid subscriber. I suppose it could be a good gateway app but if youre serious about mindfulness you will likely move on (and be happy about it) when you get sick of this one’s annoying features. Its a meditation app for pop culture.

reviews.title: Rewinding is a paid feature now??? Adios Insight Timer
reviews.text:
Tl;dr: This app has become unusable at the free tier. And I refuse to use/support this app as long as this is the pay-to-play business model being implemented. 

(details in full review below) 

I’ve always enjoyed this app. And I saw value in the premium features. But it used to still be of value to the free users. 
Making it a thing that Rewind and Time Scrub/Timestamp Selection are a pay to play thing takes a LOT away from free users. 
After meditations, I would often go back to certain spots and listen to key words/moments so I could remember important stuff I wanted/needed to journal about. 
With my brain traumas, this had become an integral part of any guided meditations. 

I haven’t used apps for meditation for a while, and am looking to get an app again for it. 

This app ain’t it. 
Y’all are taking stuff away from people who need it and may not have the means to pay for premium. So even when I have the means to go premium, I won’t. Because I refuse to support this business model.

reviews.title: Insight into Gamification
reviews.text: I used this app for many years when it was just a simple timer. I was very happy with its clean interface, sounds and ease of use. Then, it went all infantile and gamified: stats, check-ins, streaks, etc. Even in a practice like meditation, you can't be distracted from distraction by the distraction these app developers insist upon. Very depressing.

reviews.title: So difficult to find anything
reviews.text: Used this app for six years, and it’s now virtually impossible to discover new content on the app, the filters are so limited, not meaningful and there’s no sort available. I listen to the same handful of meditations now because it’s designed in a way that is too aggravating to explore or even find content on a specific topic. Even finding meditations I previously listened to is a nightmare scrolling exercise now - the irony of being frustrated using an app intended to help you relax. Really disappointing to see the user experience deteriorate so much., it used to be one of my favorite apps.

reviews.title: Worst app ever
reviews.text: After 2+ years this morning it decided to wipe out my entire history and start over, absolutely done with this

reviews.title: cancelling my subscription
reviews.text: insight app used to be my gold standard meditation app, but every update makes it less like a meditation app and more like a social media platform. Ever since they added the video feature, when you open the app instead of calming images, you now get awful aggressively extroverted self-promoting headshots. This engagement attempt visually jarring and I’m using this app less and less because I can’t stand opening it and seeing these thumbnails anymore. There is no option to disable the video thumbs (and video feature) or customise the layout. It’s also poor taste and off-putting to demand a rating from paid subscribers and suggest tips immediately afterwards. All of these behaviours are counterintuitive to meditation.

I have used the app for 8 years and listened to 1,439 FREE tracks.

NOW, it monitors how many times I listen to a track and then won’t let me listen to it unless I buy a subscription!!!

A message pops up and says I need to purchase a subscription!! 

I DO NOT RECOMMEND IT ANY LONGER, and will be finding a new app.

reviews.title: SEARCH IS AWFUL
reviews.text: I have been using this app since 2012 and have recommended it to many friends. Regretfully, the support and the search features have only gotten worse and the search is complete rubbish. I want to love this app again, but need the search function to work properly.

reviews.title: Please stop making it more convoluted
reviews.text: This app used to be so simple, so clean and so easy to use. Now, I have to fumble through a bunch of features I don’t care about. This is a meditation and yoga app, not Pinterest for the soul. Why are “Editor’s picks” displayed prominently in two separate places? Why isn’t there an option to simply not to view those? Why isn’t there an option to clean up the view and disable the unwanted portions? The homepage isn’t even items I chose. Bookmarks and playlists should be on the homepage, as should events I signed up for. Signing up for a trial of Plus is also a headache too. It’s far too easy for Insight Timer to just charge you before your trial is up and it’s difficult to cancel membership. Please fix your app, stop giving people what they didn’t ask you for and make your app user friendly.

reviews.title: Great meditations; makes phone hot!
reviews.text: Still makes my iPhone 17 Pro very hot. Reported about a year ago but no change. Doesn’t seem to matter what track I play; gets hot after just a few minutes. No other app causes this. …

reviews.title: The worlds largest Free mental health app - for an annual fee of £35
reviews.text: The listing is misleading because it states that the service is free. In reality, it only includes a 7-day free trial, after which an annual charge applies. This should be made clearer in the description.

reviews.title: Bigger isn’t better
reviews.text: Still no way to mark the tracks or teachers I don’t like. Bigger isn’t better. Update: Did I just get a pop up about new live yoga right after I started my meditation timer? Yes. Yes, I did. Um, can’t the ads wait until after I’ve done my sitting practice? Updated review: some of the changes are good, but I think now that I've been using guided meditations more I've noticed places for improvement. First - it no longer switches to landscape view on the iPad - that's a small thing but it used to so now it's just frustrating. More importantly, to get to my bookmarked meditations, I have to go through something like 5 screens, many of them with very bright white backgrounds. In the dark morning this is very off putting. Finally, still, no download option means you have to be connected to the internet. I still love Insight Timer. The changes are great! One thing I would change: you can't rate a guided mediation unless you listen all the way thru. This means that 1)of course all the ratings are high bc who's going to sit thru 60 minutes of a bad mediation to rate it? and 2) there's no way to track those I've tried and didn't like. I wish there was some way to track negative ones as well as good ones. Older: This app has really helped me develop a meditation routine. Very dedicated customer service.

reviews.title: doesn’t work offline
reviews.text: No reason for a timer app to not work offline. To use even the basic timer without an internet connection you have to pay for a subscription.

reviews.title: Price change in less than an hour
reviews.text: I downloaded this app and it offered me a free trial for a week then if I chose to keep it I would need to pay £35 for the year. I skipped it preferring to just try the free resources. An hour later after using one of the meditations I was offered a free trial for a month, branded as a ‘gift’, however, if I chose this option the yearly payment would be £55! That didn’t do much for my anxiety and stress!!

reviews.title: 7 prompts after completing a meditation
reviews.text: Just completed a meditation and received 7 prompts: update your goal, share, record how you feel, upgrade… wow. Will be looking for another tool. Shame, used to be a great app.

reviews.title: Stop forcing me to fill out the same questionnaire
reviews.text: I’m a paid user. When I haven’t used it for a while it forces me through a long questionnaire about my goals, aims and ambitions, even forcing me to set a goal, all without being able to skip. I’ve done this maybe 5 times now with increasing frustration. I now just click blindly so the data they are fetching is useless anyway. I have cancelled my subscription.

reviews.title: Forcing video into my mindfulness practice? Absolutely not.
reviews.text:
As someone who works in media, I’m keenly aware of how insidious the “pivot to video” creep has become. My favorite meditation app was the last place I expected it to show up. 

I’ve been a dedicated Insight Timer user for over a decade. It’s where I go to unplug, ground myself and literally *close my eyes.* What’s kept me loyal to IT is how calming and low-stimulation the user experience is — it used to be so simple and practical, like the Reddit of meditation apps. I loved that it never really changed. So waking up one morning to find a carousel of *meditation videos* (who is asking for these, seriously?) suddenly featured at the top of the home screen, with no way to turn the feature off, feels manipulative and totally inconsistent with the app’s original purpose. Seeing so many faces staring back at me (with sleek, professional lighting and backgrounds) when I’ve opened the app specifically to get away from that vibe grosses me out, like self-improvement is being TikTokified.

Miss me with this redesign. If there truly is a demand for video content in this space (which I find hard to fathom), there are ways to meet it without forcing the rest of us to go down the scroll hole with you. I’m taking my meditation practice elsewhere, and I hope everyone serious about their practice does too.

reviews.title: Good selection of stuff but increasingly annoying app
reviews.text: As per title there’s a lot of good stuff on this. Unfortunately it’s another app that seems to get worse. So many stupid pop ups you have to click through. I shouldn’t have to click through 4 different prompts just to end a session. No I don’t want to click I’m committed, share progress etc blablabla

reviews.title: Nefarious UX
reviews.text: I use Insight Time to help me calm down and relax after stressful days. And, largely, the meditations do exactly that. But then after the meditation, the endless clicks, animations, and questions to get back out are infuriating, negating the effect of the session. Even worse, on a regular basis it replaces the “continue” button with an “install widget” button. Here’s a thought: if I wanted the widget I would have installed it by now. Why do you think trying to trick me into putting the widget onto my phone is a good idea? It makes me want to uninstall your app, not use it more.

reviews.title: I can’t stand this app
reviews.text:
The content is great, but the app itself is beyond annoying. 

I’m a paying subscriber and use the app occasionally, maybe every two weeks. Each time I open the app I’m bombarded with a series of prompts asking me how I’m feeling, what I’m aiming towards, what my motivation is, when I like to meditate, etc. All of which I need to answer before it allows me to access the content I’m paying for. There’s no option to ignore this and I’ve un-ticked every related setting for reminders, prompts and things within the app. 

Is it too much to ask to be able to access my paid content without all this unnecessary spam? It’s ironic that this ritual actually puts me in a more agitated state of mind than I was in before opening my mindfulness app. Perhaps it’s just a disingenuous way for the developers to harvest our data? If so, I can’t imagine that data’s of great quality, because I just mash through the closest answers to get the thing to go away. 

I hope they change this feature, because it’s unfair to the many incredibly talented practitioners who produce content for this app. But if they don’t change it soon, I’ll go elsewhere for my mindfulness content.

The amount of unnecessary and unavoidable pop ups is ironically about as irritating and unmindful as possible for a meditation app. I just want to use the timer! I don’t want to commit to anything or tell you about my goals, ever!
